- When sentiment is consistently positive (≥0.67) over recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast slightly, especially after spikes.
- After a sharp price spike (e.g., >+3% from prior day), model often overshoots in next 3–5 days; apply downward correction by 1–2% of spike magnitude.
- If sentiment is negative (≤0.33) and price is trending down, model often underestimates further decline; adjust forecast downward by 0.5–1.5% per negative sentiment day.
- Model frequently overcorrects after mean-reversion periods; if price has recently moved back toward historical mean, reduce forecast bias toward mean.
- For 30-day horizon, model tends to overestimate early in the forecast window (first 5–7 days) when sentiment is volatile; dampen initial forecast values by 0.5–1.0% relative to recent history.
- If sentiment history shows alternating bullish/bearish cycles, model often misaligns with sentiment direction; align forecast slope with sentiment trend direction, not historical momentum.
